text:
Abstract
This study compares what two public repositories hold for Staphylococcus aureus: the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA, via BRC Analytics’ proxy). We queried GEO for Series (GSE) records annotated to “Staphylococcus aureus” and retrieved the total count and metadata for the first 20 Series. We queried ENA for raw sequencing runs by taxon ID 1280 (Staphylococcus aureus) and retrieved a page of 200 runs together with the total number of runs in ENA. GEO returned 500 matching Series, of which 20 were listed in the response; experiment types among these included expression profiling by high throughput sequencing, genome binding/occupancy profiling, non-coding RNA profiling, and records labeled “Other.” ENA reported 181,408 total Staphylococcus aureus runs, of which 200 were returned in our page; observed library strategies included whole genome sequencing (WGS) and bisulfite sequencing. Across the 20 GEO Series, sample_count ranged from 2 to 44; across the 200 ENA runs, read_count ranged from 0 to 21,120,710 in our sample. These results clarify that GEO primarily holds processed, curated transcriptomic and functional profiling data with study-level context, while ENA broadly holds raw sequencing data at run level, dominated by WGS. The comparison informs researchers about data scope and retrieval pathways for downstream analyses of S. aureus.

I. Introduction
Background. Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive bacterium and human pathogen widely studied for its virulence, resistance mechanisms, and genomic diversity. Understanding repository coverage helps plan analyses that require processed expression matrices versus raw sequencing data.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. Before these queries, the relative scope and data types available for Staphylococcus aureus in GEO vs. ENA were not quantified in this session.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: to quantify and contrast repository coverage and data types for S. aureus in GEO and ENA. Hypothesis: ENA holds a larger number of raw sequencing runs, while GEO concentrates curated study-level functional profiling records.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We performed a two-resource comparison: GEO for processed functional profiling studies (Series) and ENA for raw sequencing runs. GEO was chosen for its processed expression/transcriptomics records; ENA for raw FASTQ runs.

Materials.
- NCBI GEO via functions.geo_search
- ENA via BRC Analytics proxy via functions.brc_ena_runs

Procedures.
- GEO: functions.geo_search with arguments organism="Staphylococcus aureus", entry_type="gse", max_results=20.
- ENA: functions.brc_ena_runs with arguments taxonomy_id="1280", limit=200, offset=0.

Statistical Analysis.
- GEO total_count (500) and returned (20) were taken directly from the GEO query’s total_count and returned fields. The percent returned was computed as 20/500 = 4.0%. Experiment_type categories were enumerated across the 20 returned records; unique categories observed were counted (4). Sample_count min and max were computed from the ‘sample_count’ field across the 20 records (min=2; max=44).
- ENA total_in_ena (181,408) and returned (200) were taken from the ENA response fields. The percent returned was computed as 200/181,408 ≈ 0.110%. Library_strategy categories were enumerated across the 200 returned runs; unique categories observed were counted (2: WGS, Bisulfite-Seq). Read_count min and max were computed across the 200 runs (min=0; max=21,120,710). All category counts reflect only the returned page, not global distributions.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1. Repository coverage and observed data types for Staphylococcus aureus.

| Source | Matched entity type | Organism filter used | Total matches (field) | Returned in this query | Percent returned | Observed assay/data types in returned set |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GEO | Series (GSE) | “Staphylococcus aureus” | 500 (total_count) | 20 | 4.0% | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing; Genome binding/occupancy profiling; Non-coding RNA profiling; Other |
| ENA | Runs (FASTQ) | Taxon 1280 | 181,408 (total_in_ena) | 200 | 0.110% | WGS; Bisulfite-Seq |

Table 2. Range of record-level sizes in returned subsets.

| Source | Measure | Minimum observed | Maximum observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| GEO (20 Series) | sample_count | 2 | 44 |
| ENA (200 runs) | read_count | 0 | 21,120,710 |

Findings.
- GEO matched 500 Series; 20 were returned; percent returned was 4.0%.
- ENA matched 181,408 runs; 200 were returned; percent returned was 0.110%.
- GEO experiment_types in the returned set included four categories.
- ENA library_strategies in the returned set included two categories.
- GEO sample_count ranged from 2 to 44 across the returned Series.
- ENA read_count ranged from 0 to 21,120,710 across the returned runs.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The numbers indicate that ENA holds far more raw sequencing runs for S. aureus than GEO holds study-level Series, as expected for repositories with different scopes. GEO’s Series reflect curated, processed functional datasets; ENA’s runs reflect raw sequencing submissions dominated by WGS.

Context. GEO Series metadata listed experiment types including expression profiling, genome binding/occupancy profiling, and non-coding RNA profiling. ENA runs in the returned page showed library strategies WGS and bisulfite sequencing, with instruments including NovaSeq 6000, HiSeq 2500, and MiSeq.

Limitations. GEO’s response was truncated to 20 Series; ENA’s response was one page of 200 runs. Category counts reflect only the returned subsets, not full distributions. GEO’s processed expression values are not embedded in the API metadata and require downloading supplementary files from FTP. ENA content was accessed via a proxy; results reflect ENA’s dataset but are paged.

Conclusion & Future Directions. GEO provides curated functional profiling Series for S. aureus (500 Series total), while ENA holds extensive raw sequencing runs (181,408 total). Future queries could facet ENA by library_strategy to quantify RNA-Seq versus WGS, and expand GEO retrieval to list all Series or to filter by experiment type. We can also produce downloadable tables summarizing GEO Series and ENA run counts on request.

References
[1] NCBI GEO (GSE search). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi?db=gds&term=%22Staphylococcus%20aureus%22%5BOrganism%5D%20AND%20%22gse%22%5BFilter%5D&retmax=20
[2] BRC Analytics ENA proxy (Taxonomy 1280 runs). https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/1280?limit=200

Acknowledgments
We thank NCBI GEO for Series metadata and BRC Analytics for ENA proxy access to raw sequencing run records.
